title: Holiness is for you
hookLine: the universal call is addressed to you by name
tomorrow: what does the last line of Mass actually tell you to do?
last: PEACE FIRST · LITTLE THINGS, GREAT LOVE.

lines: A CLUB WITH A DRESS CODE?
cards: Saints sound like a club with a dress code: halos, visions, a convent, ideally a miracle or two. Fine for them. Not for someone who forgets to call their grandmother back.
The Second Vatican Council answered that hunch in one of its documents on the Church, with a whole chapter on the call to holiness. And it is addressed to a surprisingly long list of people.

teach.b: The Council says that everyone who follows Christ, whatever their state or walk of life, is called to the fullness of Christian life and the perfection of love. Not priests and nuns first and the rest later. Everyone.

teach.h: THIS IS THE WILL OF GOD.
teach.b: Paul said it plainly to a young church, in the Douay-Rheims: "For this is the will of God, your sanctification." Your holiness. And the call isn't a mass email.
Through Isaiah, God says to his people: "fear not, for I have redeemed thee, and called thee by thy name: thou art mine." By name.

Pope Francis gave it a phrase worth telling a friend tonight: the saints next door, parents raising children with love, people working to support their families, the sick, elderly religious who keep smiling.
That's yesterday's portrait, drawn in ordinary faces. Look back down this week: none of it needed a halo.

how: Catholics speak of the universal call to holiness, taught by the Second Vatican Council in Lumen Gentium; on All Saints' Day they remember the saints no calendar names.

games.q: what does “holiness is for you” mean?
o: the Church's process for naming official saints
everyone, in every walk of life, is called to be a saint
a special calling given to priests and religious

games.q: the week near the top — tap the pairs.

s: the call to holiness is mainly for priests and nuns
the Council says everyone who follows Christ, whatever their walk of life, is called.
Pope Francis wrote about the saints next door
parents, workers, the sick: ordinary holiness.
you have to work a miracle to be a saint
the call is to the perfection of love; the saints next door never make a list.

games.q: a friend who works two jobs and raises a kid says, "holiness is for people with time to pray all day." what did the Council say?
o: "true; you can start once life slows down."
"you're called too, in exactly that life."
"only if you join a religious order."
games.why: the Second Vatican Council taught that everyone, whatever their state or walk of life, is called to holiness. Francis named people like her: the saints next door.

practice: Close your eyes and listen for the way someone who loves you says your name: a parent, a grandparent, an old friend. Hear it said once, warmly, and let the sit hold it.
If you pray, you can let Isaiah's words follow it: called thee by thy name, thou art mine.

wordCard.voice: Holiness is for you. The universal call: everyone, in every walk of life, called to love, and called by name.

carryVoice: Hold on to this: you, by name, a call addressed to you and not to somebody holier. Next week, the last climb.
